notes: The code change matches the reference for both zip and squashfs: symlinks are skipped with a notice naming -l/--links, exposed with the .rclonelink suffix when the flag is on, NewObject agrees with List, and range reads are clamped. Tests cover the zip and squashfs symlink paths, a regular .rclonelink file, and an end-to-end hostile-archive escape; the docs addition is relevant, though range/seek reads are not tested.

The source changes match the reference exactly. The candidate adds good tests: zip and squashfs symlink handling with and without `--links`, a regular file ending in `.rclonelink` (squashfs only), and an end-to-end hostile-archive escape check. Range/seek reads are not tested, and the docs section is a small relevant extra.

The non-test code matches the reference fix exactly: it extracts literal placeholder names from the checked CEL AST and only runs response retry matching when a response placeholder or a dynamic name is present. The tests cover the ph() form and the required request-only cases (method, upstream.host, an escaped literal, and a near-miss name like status_codes), but nothing exercises the dynamic-name path or Placeholders() directly.

The non-test code matches the reference: placeholder names are pulled from the checked CEL AST, a dynamic name returns an empty string, and only exact response placeholders or the header prefix trigger response retries. The tests cover each spec case (request-only, upstream.host, escaped literal, status_codes look-alike, ph() call); the dynamic-name case is not tested.

The source change matches the reference fix: an atomic closed flag makes a repeat Close return net.ErrClosed, the refcount decrement, close, map delete and unlink all run under the mutex, the dup'd file is closed, and abstract sockets are never unlinked. The tests cover multi-holder unlink timing, double close, close racing a relisten, and abstract names for both unix and unixgram; the only nit is that the abstract test creates temp files in the package directory.

The source change is identical to the reference: it closes the dup'd fd and serializes Close under the map lock. A CAS guard makes a second Close return net.ErrClosed, and abstract sockets are never unlinked. The added tests cover last-holder unlinking, double close, the close/relisten race and abstract-name safety, for both unix and unixgram.

Fixes the root cause by making the header parser strip any single-component prefix, falling back to rename/copy-to and a matching-halves `diff --git` split. It also routes the prefix overrides through `AddCommonDiffArgs`, which covers every display diff, and catches the `stash show | apply -R` pipe. However, it forces `diff.mnemonicPrefix=false`, overriding the user's display preference, which the maintainer's intent and the reference deliberately preserve.

Fixes the parser to accept any single-component prefix, adds rename-to/copy-to handling, and forces a/ b/ on every diff lazygit runs (including the stash-show pipe into `git apply`), but it also sets `diff.mnemonicPrefix=false`, which needlessly overrides the user's chosen display prefixes. Folding the configs into AddCommonDiffArgs is tidy but touches more call sites and test expectations than needed; the visible tests are mostly argv updates plus a builder test, and the truncated diff hides any parser tests.

The wrapper changes match the reference exactly, and the plugin closes the connection on both field and table failures, logging any close error, which is slightly cleaner than the reference ignoring it. The tests check the engine-ID reset on reconnect, that an open connection keeps its engine ID, and that a failed gather closes the connection. The unrelated edit to the TestSnmpInitGosmi path is a minor scope issue, and the package-suite failure looks environmental rather than caused by the fix.

The wrapper changes match the reference exactly: Close is added to the interface, Get/Walk reconnect first, and Reconnect clears the USM engine ID, boots and time before connecting again. snmp.go closes the connection on top-level or table errors and logs any Close error via s.Log, which may be what broke the package suite if a test leaves Log nil. The added tests are useful, but it also changes TestSnmpInitGosmi to a relative path to work around its local environment, an unrelated edit.

Fixes the root cause by making `cancelOneJob` re-aggregate a reusable caller that has children instead of force-writing it as Cancelled; this does not depend on ID ordering, and the patch emits a concurrency re-check when cancelling updates no job. It also makes `RefreshReusableCallerStatus` refresh the run on every child update even when the caller is unchanged: a defensible safety net that goes beyond the reference and adds per-update DB work. Two minor issues: the caller is returned as 'updated' even when its status did not change, and one test comment wrongly claims ascending IDs, yet the three added tests cover nesting, runner acknowledgement and blocked-run emission well.

Fixes the root cause: reusable callers with children are re-aggregated from their children instead of being set to cancelled directly, so they stay cancelling until the runner acknowledges, and the cascade then settles the callers, attempt and run. It also fixes the blocked concurrency group by emitting the run when the cancel updates no jobs. Two deviations from the reference: it adds a defensive run refresh in RefreshReusableCallerStatus on every child update where the caller is unchanged (extra hot-path work), and it emits whenever no jobs were updated rather than only when the run status actually changed. The tests are strong: nested callers through the runner acknowledgement, the legacy stuck state, and a mocked emit check.

This is a working alternative design: during head GC it asks the exemplar storage, through a new optional interface, whether the series has an exemplar at or after minValidTime, then keeps the series identity, releases its chunks and appender, and fixes mmapReady and chunk metrics. Calling into exemplar storage under stripe and series locks creates a cross-component lock-ordering hazard, which forced a ChunkSnapshot refactor that buffers all exemplars in memory. Unlike the reference, it does not protect exemplars that are appended but not yet committed. The tests are thorough, covering all three compaction paths, both appender APIs, snapshot on and off, two restart rounds, chunk metrics, head MinTime, and zero/negative timestamps.

Instead of storing the newest exemplar timestamp on each series, the patch asks the exemplar storage through an optional interface whether to retain a series, during both ordinary GC and selected/stale GC; it correctly releases chunks, the appender and mmap-ready counts, survives replay and snapshot restore, and spotted and fixed the new lock-order risk in ChunkSnapshot. Weaknesses: exemplars appended but not yet committed are unprotected, which the reference handles; GC is now coupled to exemplar storage locks; and the ChunkSnapshot restructuring widens the scope, though the tests are very thorough.
